topics.title: Greenland security deal advances
topics.summary: Denmark and Greenland reacted cautiously to a new U.S.-Greenland security arrangement that would expand American Arctic military access while keeping Danish sovereignty intact.
topics.discussionPrompt: If Greenland gets more security attention without changing flags, who calls that clever diplomacy and who still wants to read every footnote?

topics.title: China stockpiles steady oil markets
topics.summary: Oil prices remain volatile, but analysts say China's large reserves and lower imports have helped prevent sharper spikes during the Iran conflict.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a country's oil stash calms everyone else's prices, who admires the planning and who wonders what else is sitting in storage?

topics.title: Riyadh missile attack intercepted
topics.summary: Saudi Arabia said it intercepted a Houthi ballistic missile aimed at Riyadh, adding to fears that Yemen's renewed fighting could threaten regional shipping and energy routes.
topics.discussionPrompt: If one intercepted missile can make airports, oil markets, and diplomats nervous, who starts with the map and who starts with the group chat?

topics.title: Voter groups face funding gaps
topics.summary: U.S. voter registration and turnout groups warn that reduced donations and staffing could limit outreach as the 2026 midterms get underway.
topics.discussionPrompt: When civic groups have fewer people and less money, who worries about turnout and who thinks campaigns will find new ways to reach voters?

topics.title: AI worries get practical
topics.summary: The Guardian answered reader questions about AI risks, emphasizing misuse, regulation, industry incentives, and everyday accountability over simple doomsday framing.
topics.discussionPrompt: If AI fear gets turned into practical questions, who wants rules right now and who says everyone needs to stop naming everything a robot apocalypse?

topics.title: Australia debates AI readiness
topics.summary: Australian leaders and commentators are pressing for clearer AI policy as concerns grow over misinformation, copyright, youth safety, and tech company power.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a country admits the technology is moving faster than the rules, who drafts a policy memo and who asks whether anyone read the last one?

topics.title: Sydney metro stations reopen soon
topics.summary: New South Wales officials said ten historic Sydney train stations will reopen as part of the Sydenham to Bankstown metro extension.
topics.discussionPrompt: When old stations come back with a metro upgrade, who gets nostalgic about the platforms and who just wants the train to arrive on time?

topics.title: Vanderbilt wins on final mistake
topics.summary: Vanderbilt stunned NC State after a late fumble on an intentional-safety attempt, turning a 17-point deficit into a wild 35-31 win.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a game flips because the safest play goes wrong, who calls it destiny and who refuses to relax during any final ten seconds ever again?

topics.title: Weekend culture calendar fills up
topics.summary: A Guardian entertainment guide highlighted new films, concerts, stage shows, games, albums, and streaming releases arriving across the week.
topics.discussionPrompt: When one week has too many shows, games, and albums, who makes a schedule and who picks whatever has the best snacks nearby?

topics.title: Sports gambling scrutiny grows
topics.summary: CBS News examined the rapid growth of online sports betting and lawsuits questioning how major platforms design and market their apps.
topics.discussionPrompt: If betting apps feel like entertainment until the bill arrives, who blames personal choices and who wants the app design put on trial?
